# 1g Retirement, server list, Phase 1 exit: contract

**Read first:** [server retirement](../processes/servers/server-retirement.md), [servers module → Server list, Lifecycle](../modules/servers.md#server-list), [roadmap → Phase 1 exit](../roadmap.md#phase-1-servers), designs `RP-Servers`, `RP-Server-overview`, `RP-Phone-server`, the 0e notes on `ForgetSubject`, every Phase 1 **As built**.

**Done when:** a server can be retired from provisioning, failed or active, with the consequences dialog and type-the-name confirmation; the job cancels running provisioning, removes the stack when chosen and reachable, deletes only Proxier's own DNS records, erases generated values and forgets the host key; retired servers are read-only and hidden by default; the server list has every column, filter and bulk action of the module doc; the server page works at phone width; the Phase 1 exit demo passes on the real deployment; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Dialog | Strength 3: the subscriptions and links from `UsageReader` (Phase 1: "Subscriptions aren't built yet"), the DNS records that will be deleted (from `servers_dns_records`, not deleted), **Remove the stack from the server** (checked when the latest self-check reached SSH, or the server is provisioning/failed with a deployment; unchecked and disabled when nothing was uploaded), the name to type. The button stays disabled until the typed name matches (client-side, and checked again on the server). | retirement.md step 1. |
| Immediate effects | `POST /servers/:id/retire`, one `Write`: enqueue `servers.retire` (payload `{server_id, remove_stack}`) and set `retire_job_id`. From then on the server is **retiring**: pages show "Retiring…", every action is disabled, rounds skip it, `EndpointCatalog` no longer lists it. `ServerHostnames` keeps listing it until `retired`, because its DNS still points to it. | retirement.md: "stops being offered to subscriptions at once, and its checks stop". |
| Job type | `servers.retire`: queue `provisioning`, `MaxAttempts 3` (backoff 1 min, 5 min), **no resource key on enqueue** (it must start while provisioning holds it). Steps `cancel-provisioning`, `remove-stack`, `dns`, `finish`. | |
| cancel-provisioning | `jobs.Cancel` (actor = this job) every **queued** job with resource key `server:<id>` (they would fail on a retiring server anyway) and a **running** `servers.provision` of the server; then wait (poll every 1 s, up to 15 min, selecting on this job's own cancellation) until no job holds `server:<id>` (a running redeploy or check finishes normally). Cancelling provisioning is quick because its waiting steps (DNS wait, `wait-http`, smoke-test retries) watch `r.Cancelling()` (README rule); the 15 min only covers a long non-waiting command such as the Docker install. Running out → the step fails ("server:12 is still busy with job #N") and the job's attempts retry. | retirement.md step 3.1. |
| remove-stack | When chosen: connect (5 s dial timeout here); unreachable, auth refused or host key changed → log "skipped: unreachable (<reason>)" and continue with `stack_removed: false`. Reachable → the version's `uninstall` steps, then `sudo -n rm -rf -- <dir>` (only when `dir` is absolute, not `/`, and at least two levels deep — the manifest check already enforces the first two). | retirement.md step 3.2. |
| dns | For each not-yet-deleted record: `Driver.Remove`. Removed → `deleted_at`. Kept → `kept = reason`. Cloudflare errors fail the step (retried by the job's attempts). | |
| finish | One `Write`: state `retired`, `retired_at`, `health = NULL` and every health field cleared, generated values **deleted**, endpoints deleted, `server.retired{dns_removed, dns_kept, stack_removed}`. After the commit (not in the transaction): `SSH.ForgetSubject(ctx, "server:<id>", actor)`. A crash between them is healed by the step re-running: `finish` on an already retired server only calls `ForgetSubject`. | ADR 0012; 0e note. |
| Failure | `OnFailed` (after the attempts): `server.retire_failed{step, error}` (new, **on**). The server **stays retiring**: `state` is unchanged (active, failed or provisioning) but `retire_job_id` is still set, so checks stay off, `EndpointCatalog` still leaves it out and every action stays disabled, because the stack may already be gone. The page shows "Retirement failed at <step>: <error>" with **Retry retirement** only. Retry, in one `Write`: `jobs.System.RetryWithTx` (1d) and `retire_job_id` = the new job. | Not in events.md yet; a stuck retirement must be visible, and a half-retired server must not come back into service. |
| Read-only | A retired server's page: header with "retired on <date>", Overview (identity, history), Stack (the deployment history rows only: kind, versions, state, time, job link; **no file content, no Reveal, no Diff**), Jobs, Activity. No actions. Every action handler refuses retired servers (409), and so do the Stack file and diff routes. | retirement.md: erased values "can't be shown or served again". Deployed files hold the old credentials in clear inside the seal, and masking needs the erased values, so neither content nor a diff can be shown safely. |
| Deployed files after retirement | Kept, sealed and never shown, until their deployments are pruned — Phase 1 does **not** prune deployments; noted in data-model retention as "kept". | retirement.md "until the deployments are pruned"; no pruning rule exists yet. |
| Server list | Columns per modules/servers.md#server-list: flag + name, health badge + since, lifecycle (when not active), IP, proxy hostname, template version ("update available" when the default is newer), last proxy test first-byte ms, CPU / memory / disk bars (latest sample), traffic today, subscriptions count (`UsageReader`, "—" in Phase 1). Filters (`ui.FilterForm`, in the URL): lifecycle (default everything but retired; "show retired"), health, location, template. Sorting by name (default), health, traffic today. | |
| Bulk actions | Row checkboxes + "select all on this page": **Run checks now** (each server), **Upgrade to default version** (the rollout screen of 1e), **Pause checks** (the pause dialog for many). Disabled when the selection holds a non-active server, with the reason. | modules/servers.md. |
| Phone | Under 760 px the list becomes cards (name, health, reason, since) and the server page stacks its header actions into the "more" menu, with Overview and Health first (RP-Phone-server). | ui/README "reacting to a notification". |
| Name reuse | Re-run 1d's `TestNamesAreNeverReused` through the real retire flow. | |

## Go signatures

```go
package retire

type Consequences struct {
	Subscriptions []string
	Links         int
	UsageKnown    bool
	DNS           []dns.Record
	StackPossible bool // something was uploaded
	StackDefault  bool // reachable at the last self-check
}
func (s *Service) Consequences(ctx context.Context, serverID int64) (Consequences, error)
func (s *Service) Retire(ctx context.Context, serverID int64, typedName string, removeStack bool, actor string) (jobID int64, err error) // ErrNameMismatch
func (s *Service) JobType() jobs.Type
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /servers/:id/retire` | Dialog |
| `POST /servers/:id/retire` | Start → server page |
| `POST /servers/:id/retire/retry` | Retry a failed retirement |
| `GET /servers?state=&health=&location=&template=&sort=` | Full list |
| `POST /servers/bulk/checks`, `/servers/bulk/pause` | Bulk actions; upgrade posts to 1e's rollout plan |

## Events

New: `server.retire_failed{step, error}` (on, 🔴). Recorded: `server.retired`, `ssh.host_forgotten` (by sshx, per pinned address).

## Phase 1 exit demo

Run on `proxier.tikhonnnnn.com` and write the result into **As built** (the steps the user must do by hand are listed for them, not done by Claude):

1. Settings → Integrations → Cloudflare: token, zone `tikhonnnnn.com`.
2. Servers → **New server**: a fresh VPS (IP, root password), location `nl` suggested, seed template → watch provisioning to **active**; the name is `nl-2` (or the next free number); `server.activated` arrives in Telegram.
3. Import the URI into a phone app; it connects.
4. First check round → `healthy`.
5. On the home router, block 443 to the server's IP from home only. After two rounds → `blocked` with the reason naming nodes abroad; Telegram 🟣. Remove the rule → `healthy`; Telegram 🟢.
6. **Rotate credentials** → the URI changes; the old URI stops working in the app; the new one works.
7. Record in As built what passed and what didn't; update the roadmap's Phase 1 line and `CLAUDE.md` Phase status.

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/events.md`: `server.retire_failed`; `server.retired` payload gains `dns_kept`.
- `docs/data-model.md#retention`: deployments and deployed files of retired servers are kept (no pruning yet).
- `docs/processes/servers/server-retirement.md`: the job's retries and `server.retire_failed`; a failed retirement leaves the server retiring (out of service) with **Retry retirement**; queued jobs of the server are cancelled; `ServerHostnames` keeps a retiring server until retired; deployed files of a retired server are kept sealed and never shown or diffed.
- `docs/roadmap.md`: Phase 1 done (date) once the exit demo passed, with what is left.

## Checklist

Retirement, in `retire/retire_test.go` (Harness):

- [ ] Active, reachable, stack removal checked → `compose down -v`, `dir` deleted, DNS deleted, retired; `EndpointCatalog` no longer lists it — `TestRetireReachableServer`
- [ ] Unreachable → stack step skipped and logged; DNS deleted; retired — `TestRetireUnreachableServer`
- [ ] DNS record changed by hand to point elsewhere → kept; `dns_removed: false` for it — `TestRetireKeepsForeignRecord`
- [ ] Retire during running provisioning → provisioning cancelled first, then retirement continues — `TestRetireCancelsProvisioning`
- [ ] Failed server that stopped before DNS → no DNS to delete; retired — `TestRetireFailedBeforeDNS`
- [ ] Wrong typed name → refused (handler) and the button disabled (page) — `TestRetireNameMustMatch`
- [ ] After retiring `nl-2`, a new server in `nl` → `nl-3` — `TestNamesAreNeverReusedAfterRetire`
- [ ] Generated values and endpoints erased; deployed files kept; host key forgotten (`ssh.host_forgotten`) — `TestRetireErasesSecretsAndForgetsHost`
- [ ] A retired server's page has no actions; every action endpoint answers 409; the Stack tab lists deployments but its file and diff routes answer 409 and no response contains the old UUID — `TestRetiredServerIsReadOnly`
- [ ] A queued redeploy is cancelled by the retirement; a running self-check is waited for — `TestRetireCancelsQueuedJobs`
- [ ] Rounds skip a retiring server; `ServerHostnames` keeps it until retired — `TestRetiringServerStopsChecks`
- [ ] Cloudflare fails three times → `server.retire_failed`; the server stays retiring (no checks, not in the catalog, only **Retry retirement**); Retry finishes it — `TestRetireFailureAndRetry`
- [ ] A crash after `finish`'s commit → the re-run only forgets the host — `TestFinishIsIdempotent`

Subscription-side edge cases of retirement.md ("removed from its subscriptions", "a subscription whose only server is retired serves ⚠️ No servers yet") are Phase 2's; they are listed in Phase 2's contract.

Server list, in `pages/servers_test.go`:

- [ ] Default filter hides retired; "show retired" reveals; filters combine and stay in the URL — `TestServerListFilters`
- [ ] Columns render with and without samples; "update available" when the default is newer — `TestServerListColumns`
- [ ] Bulk Run checks / Pause act on every selected active server; a selection with a failed server disables them — `TestBulkActions`
- [ ] Phone layout renders cards (narrow template variant present, no inline style) — `TestServerListPhone`

Manual, recorded in As built:

- [ ] The Phase 1 exit demo above.
